query: Protocol for negative-selection isolation of untouched human eosinophils from peripheral blood
title: Isolation of Human Eosinophils
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for negative-selection isolation of untouched human eosinophils from peripheral blood

### Overview

This protocol details the negative-selection isolation of untouched human eosinophils from peripheral blood. The process involves reagent preparation, granulocyte isolation via dextran sedimentation and Ficoll-Paque density gradient centrifugation, optional erythrocyte lysis, cell counting, and magnetic negative selection to purify eosinophils while minimizing activation.

### Materials/Reagents

- Separation medium: 0.5% (w/v) OVA in HBSS without Ca2+, Mg2+, or phenol red (4°C); alternatively, PBS with 2% FBS.
- 0.2% (w/v) fast green (Sigma-Aldrich) in 70% ethanol.
- 0.5% (w/v) neutral red (Sigma-Aldrich) in distilled water.
- Acidified sodium citrate.
- 6% Dextran 70 in 0.9% NaCl (or Hetastarch).
- Ficoll-Paque.
- HBSS (room temperature and 4°C).
- 0.2% NaCl and 1.6% NaCl for erythrocyte lysis.
- Antibody cocktail for human eosinophil negative selection.
- Magnetic colloid.
- Fast green/neutral red stain or Hema 3 stain for purity assessment.

### Equipment

- 60-ml syringes equipped with 19-G butterfly needles.
- Biosafety sharp container.
- Sterile 50-ml conical tubes.
- Benchtop refrigerated centrifuge for 50-ml conical tubes.
- Hemacytometer.
- Negative selection columns and magnetic separation apparatus with 3-way Luer stopcock assembly.
- 21-G needle.

### Safety & Sterility

- Use aseptic technique throughout, particularly during plasma collection and Ficoll-Paque steps.
- Dispose of needles in a biosafety sharp container.
- Perform dextran sedimentation inside a tissue culture hood.
- Maintain cells on ice and use 4°C solutions from the pellet processing stage forward to minimize eosinophil activation.
- Avoid vigorous vortexing during erythrocyte lysis to minimize cell damage.
- Ensure stainless steel mesh in the column does not become dry.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-Experiment Setup

1. Prepare separation medium consisting of 0.5% (w/v) OVA in HBSS without Ca2+, Mg2+, or phenol red at 4°C; alternatively, use PBS with 2% FBS available from StemCell Technologies. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare 0.2% (w/v) fast green (Sigma-Aldrich) in 70% ethanol and store up to 1 month at room temperature in a polypropylene tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare 0.5% (w/v) neutral red (Sigma-Aldrich) in distilled water and store up to 1 month at room temperature in a polypropylene tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->

## Granulocyte Isolation

### Blood Collection

1. Draw 40 ml of blood from a human donor by venipuncture using a 60-ml syringe equipped with a 19-G butterfly needle pre-filled with 10 ml of acidified sodium citrate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Retract the plunger with minimal traction until the syringe is filled to the 50-ml mark, then remove the syringe and attach successive additional syringes (pre-filled with the same solution) to the butterfly, repeating the drawing of blood until the desired amount has been obtained. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Remove the needle from the final syringe and place it in a biosafety sharp container. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Activated platelets stick to eosinophils; use a large-bore needle and larger amounts of acidified sodium citrate to prevent platelet activation, and aspirate blood with minimal traction to avoid shear forces. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->

### Dextran Sedimentation

1. Add 10 ml of 6% Dextran 70 in 0.9% NaCl to each syringe and gently invert 8 times to mix the dextran with the blood (Hetastarch may be used as an alternative). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. Let the syringes stand upright on their plungers for 45 to 60 min at room temperature inside a tissue culture hood. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->

### Plasma Collection

1. Express the upper granulocyte-rich plasma layer (approximately 15 to 25 ml) from each upright syringe by attaching a fresh 19-G butterfly needle (with the needle tip removed) to the syringe and pushing down on the plunger; collect the plasma in sterile 50-ml conical tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->

### Ficoll-Paque Gradient Centrifugation

1. Prepare an appropriate number of 50-ml conical polypropylene centrifuge tubes (usually one tube per 40 ml of blood drawn), each containing 23 ml of room temperature Ficoll-Paque, and overlay with 20 to 25 ml of the expressed granulocyte-rich plasma. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge using a benchtop refrigerated centrifuge for 50-ml conical tubes for 20 min at 300 × g at room temperature without using the centrifuge brake. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->

### Pellet Processing and Washing

1. Aspirate off the plasma and mononuclear layer as completely as possible from each tube, including any drops adhering to the wall, then change transfer pipets and aspirate the Ficoll-Paque layer, followed by an additional change of transfer pipets. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** When collecting cells in the remaining pellet, bring the transfer pipet all the way down to the bottom of the conical tube and avoid splashing or contact with the tube wall to minimize contamination from adherent mononuclear cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S02 -->
2. Resuspend the pellet with 1 ml HBSS using a sterile disposable transfer pipet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S03 -->
3. If more than one conical tube was loaded in the Ficoll-Paque step, pool the resuspended granulocytes from each tube in a 50-ml polypropylene centrifuge tube and bring the volume up to 50 ml with 4°C HBSS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S04 -->
4. If more than four syringes of blood were drawn, split the granulocyte yield into two 50-ml tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Keep cells on ice and use wash solutions at 4°C from this point forward to minimize eosinophil activation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S06 -->

#### Branch: Lower Density Eosinophils

1. For lower density eosinophils: Aspirate and discard only the mononuclear cell layer and plasma above it, resuspend the pellet in the Ficoll-Paque solution, transfer into a new tube, and dilute with at least an equal volume of 4°C HBSS to allow lower density eosinophils to be pelleted. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S07 -->

#### Shared continuation

1. Centrifuge the tube(s) for 5 min at 300 × g at 4°C, discard the supernatant(s), and dilute to 50 ml with 4°C HBSS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S08 -->
2. Wash the cells twice to remove any adherent platelets and density-gradient medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S09 -->

## Erythrocyte Lysis (Optional)

### Erythrocyte Lysis

1. Lyse erythrocytes by adding 23 ml of 0.2% NaCl as briefly as possible (<30 sec), then restore isotonicity by adding 23 ml of 1.6% NaCl. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Avoid vortexing the cells vigorously to minimize cell damage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
2. Centrifuge the tube(s) for 5 min at 300 × g at 4°C and wash the pellet twice with HBSS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->

## Granulocyte Counting and Preparation

### Counting and Pelleting

1. Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 300 × g at 4°C to pellet granulocytes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
2. Aspirate and discard the supernatant, loosen the pellet by gentle manual agitation, and resuspend in 1 ml separation medium per 50 × 10^6 cells; keep on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->

## Negative Selection Isolation

### Antibody Incubation

1. Add 100 μl antibody cocktail for human eosinophil negative selection per 50 × 10^6 cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Incubate the granulocyte suspension with the antibody cocktail for 20 min at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->

### Magnetic Colloid Incubation

1. For each 50 × 10^6 cells, add 60 μl magnetic colloid to the cell-antibody suspension and incubate for 20 min at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S01 -->
2. Agitate the tube periodically throughout the incubation to ensure proper mixture with antibodies. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S02 -->

### Column Preparation

1. In a cold room or 4°C refrigerated cabinet, attach a 21-G needle to the 3-way Luer stopcock assembly, place a negative selection column into the slot of the magnetic separation apparatus, and wash the column with 20 ml of separation medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T2-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Allow the fluid in the column to drop to the top level of the stainless steel mesh and close the three-way stopcock; do not allow any portion of the stainless steel mesh to become dry. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T2-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Avoid overloading the column by limiting the cell suspension to 3.0 × 10^8 magnetically bound cells per 0.5-in column and 1.5 × 10^9 cells per 0.6-in column. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T2-S04 -->

### Elution

1. Transfer the cell-antibody-colloid suspension to the top of the column, open the 3-way stopcock, and allow the cell suspension to enter the steel mesh. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T3-S01 -->
2. Once the top of the cell suspension has entered the steel mesh, begin to collect the effluent in a sterile 50-ml conical tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T3-S02 -->
3. Wash the column using 3 to 5 column volumes (12 to 20 ml) of separation medium and keep the column effluent at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T3-S03 -->

### Purity Assessment

1. Determine the number of collected cells by counting in a hemacytometer (APPENDIX 3A). Determine the purity of the cells collected by staining a cytospin preparation of the cell suspension with fast green/neutral red staining or Hema 3 staining (see Support Protocols 1 and 2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T4-S01 -->
